advisory.finding: The new test stubs _refuse_unpublishable_store with a non-raising counter and asserts only call cadence, so no test verifies that a diverged/unpublishable store actually REFUSES a batch import — the safety contract the diff claims to preserve. A regression that suppresses the gate for buffered writes (the very branch added at _seam.py:490) would leave this test green.
scenarios: A batch import runs against a tracker whose HEAD has diverged from origin/tickets so that write_blocking_divergence(tracker) returns non-None; the importer must raise CommandError and commit no chunk.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an integration test that patches rebar._store.freshness.write_blocking_divergence to return a non-None divergence dict (or constructs a genuinely diverged tracker), calls rebar.import_tickets, asserts it raises CommandError with 'ticket write refused', and asserts the commit count is unchanged (no partial chunk committed).

advisory.finding: The publishability write-guard `_refuse_unpublishable_store` was made conditional on `_batch_sink` being unset inside `finalize_event`, and re-added per flush in the importer, but the sibling batch-sink writer `enrich_drain._write_success_finalize` was not updated to re-invoke the guard before `batch_write_and_push`, so the enrich-drain finalize path now commits without the split-history publishability check.
scenarios: An enrich-drain finalize write executed against a tracker with unrecoverable split history now commits/pushes without the write-blocking-divergence refusal that formerly fired inside finalize_event.
